slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Rigid motions are defined to preserve distance: for any points A and B, A'B' = AB.

From this, rigid motions also map lines to lines, rays to rays, and segments to segments of the same length, and they preserve angle measure. We accept these, together with distance, as the basic properties of rigid motions. They also map parallel lines to parallel lines.
